history.summary: A 13th-century trikuta (triple-shrine) Hoysala temple with sanctums dedicated to Venugopala, Lakshminarasimha and Vishnu-Purushottama, built in soapstone with a stellate plan on a raised jagati. Protected monument under the Karnataka state division of the ASI. Sources differ on the patron: Wikipedia (citing Foekema/Hardy) credits Hoysala king Vira Someshwara, while karnataka.com credits Veera Narasimha, grandson of Vishnuvardhana — flag for verify. Evening timings are reported as both 4-8 PM and 6-9 PM (conflict). Town correction: the temple is in Bhadravathi (~20 km from Shivamogga), not Shimoga town. Festivals listed are typical Vaishnavite observances (verify specific calendar locally).

name: Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Temple, Bhadravathi
town_description: Bhadravathi is an industrial town about 20 km from Shivamogga, best known for the Visvesvaraya Iron and Steel Plant. It is named after the Bhadra river that flows through it, and the old town area holds the 13th-century Hoysala temple.

travel.airport: Shivamogga (Kuvempu) domestic airport (~35 km); Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru (~290 km)
travel.railway: Bhadravati railway station, in the town (Birur-Shivamogga line)
travel.road: On NH-69, ~20 km from Shivamogga and ~255 km from Bengaluru via NH-48 and Arsikere

visitor_information.best_time: October to February (20-28°C); avoid midday heat in summer
visitor_information.opening_hours: Typically 6:00 AM-1:00 PM and 4:00-8:00 PM; some sources say evenings 6:00-9:00 PM (verify locally); closed midday
